title: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)

sections.label: Social Service Offices expansion plans
sections.summary: Since 2013 there have been 24 Social Service Offices coordinating ground service delivery, and the passage asks whether there are plans to expand or scale them back.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Since 2013, we have 24 Social Service Offices, or SSOs, to coordinate the delivery of services on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Are there plans to expand or scale back the offices?

sections.label: Government and community partnerships during COVID-19
sections.summary: During COVID-19 and the circuit breaker, partnerships between the Government and community, such as the PEERS Network and Charity Food Workgroup, showed their value in meeting increased social needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: During COVID-19, especially during the circuit breaker, many of such partnerships between the Government and community demonstrated their value in meeting increased social needs, such as the PEERS Network and the Charity Food Workgroup.

sections.label: COVID-19 Recovery Grant update request
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister for an update on the recently launched COVID-19 Recovery Grant and how it helps recipients get back on their feet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: MSF most recently launched the COVID-19 Recovery Grant (CRG).

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide an update on the CRG, as well as how the CRG is designed to help its recipients get back on their feet?

sections.label: COVID-19 Recovery Grant application details
sections.summary: The passage asks MSF for an update on the COVID-19 Recovery Grant, including applications, success rates, rejection reasons, and how it helps recipients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: MSF recently launched the new COVID-19 Recovery Grant (CRG) to support lower to middle income employees and self-employed persons whose livelihoods continue to be financially impacted by the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Can MSF provide an update on the CRG – how many have applied, the average success rates, as well as reasons why applications have been rejected – and share more on how this grant is designed to help the recipients?

sections.label: Caregiver support and social sector jobs
sections.summary: The passage asks about the Ministry's plans to better support care-givers and alleviate their burdens, and for an update on social sector job creation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: What are the Ministry's plans to better support care-givers, and to alleviate some of the current burdens that they face?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Lastly, can MSF provide an update on job creation efforts in the social sector?

sections.label: ComLinks pilot for vulnerable families
sections.summary: ComLinks are piloted to bring together various service partners to provide holistic solutions to vulnerable families with children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: ComLinks are piloted to bring together various service partners to provide holistic solutions to vulnerable families with children.

sections.label: ComLink social service hubs
sections.summary: MSF announced four ComLink social service hubs at Jalan Kukoh, Marsiling, Kembangan-Chai Chee and Boon Lay to support about 1,000 rental flat families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Chairman, in 2019, MSF announced that it will be setting up four social service hubs, to be named ComLink, at Jalan Kukoh, Marsiling, Kembangan-Chai Chee and Boon Lay over the next two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: According to MSF, this pilot project announced at Committee Of Supply 2019 provides proactive and integrated support to an estimated 1,000 families living in rental flats to help them achieve sustained stability and social mobility." This includes supporting families with the potential for homeownership.

sections.label: Change for Charity Grant
sections.summary: A $20 million fund will match Community Chest donations raised through spontaneous daily acts, with businesses partnering on payment platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Under the new Change for Charity Grant, a $20 million fund will be set aside to match Community Chest’s donations raised through spontaneous acts daily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: It was also mentioned that ComChest will be partnering businesses to provide opportunities for customers to donate to Community Chest through their payment platforms.

sections.label: COVID-19 pre-school disruption
sections.summary: COVID-19 caused significant disruption for the pre-school sector, especially during the circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: COVID-19 has caused a significant amount of disruption for the pre-school sector, especially during the circuit breaker.

sections.label: ComCare poverty band-aid
sections.summary: ComCare families helped and spending have increased since inception, showing ComCare is not getting people out of poverty permanently.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Chairman, although ComCare has helped many low-income persons and challenged families and is a critical social support programme, the number of families helped and the amount spent on ComCare has not reduced, in fact increased, since its inception.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It tells me that ComCare, although it is very helpful as a support, is not getting people out of poverty permanently, and this is not a solution built to last.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Without capacity-building of families who are on ComCare, it serves only as a band-aid solution that continues to deplete our financial resources.

sections.label: Community Capability Trust timing
sections.summary: The speaker urges MSF to bring the Community Capability Trust forward to this year instead of commencing in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While I feel very encouraged by the announcement of the Community Capability Trust to help SSAs develop capacity, it will be more timely to complement the efforts of the National Jobs Council if MSF can bring this forward to this year instead of commencing only in 2022.

sections.label: SSA productivity and resilience
sections.summary: The passage asks what plans exist to help SSAs unlock productivity and strengthen resilience for social and welfare support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: To build a better eco-system of social and welfare support, what are the plans to help SSAs further unlock productivity and strengthen resilience?

sections.label: Children and Young Persons Act updates
sections.summary: In 2019 the Ministry made four updates to the Children and Young Persons Act, including amending the definition of child to include youths up to 18.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2019, the Ministry introduced four significant updates to the Children and Young Persons Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, changes were made to enhance the safeguarding of abuse on neglected children; second, the rehabilitation and re-integration of youth offenders was strengthened; third, parents with difficulties managing their children were to apply for family guidance orders replacing the formal BPC or Beyond Parental Control orders; and fourth, community resources to support vulnerable children were increased.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One of the key changes was to amend the definition of "child" to include youths, not exceeding 18 years of age in line with the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child which Singapore has signed.

sections.label: Youth-At-Risk Engagement Framework
sections.summary: In 2016 the Government put in place the Youth-At-Risk Engagement (YARE) Framework to support youth-at-risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In 2016, the Government put in place the Youth-At-Risk Engagement (YARE) Framework to support youth-at-risk (YAR).

sections.label: Youth volunteerism rates
sections.summary: According to MCCY, youth volunteerism rose from 23% in 2008 to 40% in 2018 for ages 15 to 24, and from 13% to 27% for ages 25 to 34.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
sentences.text: Chairman, according to MCCY, our youth volunteerism rate has gone up from 23% in 2008 to 40% in 2018 for youths aged between 15 and 24 years old as well as 13% in 2008 to 27% in 2018 for youths aged between 25 and 34 years old.

sections.label: Pre-school places and Sengkang
sections.summary: By around 2025, 80% of pre-schoolers can have a place in a Government supported pre-school, up from about 50% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Chairman, I understand that by around 2025, 80% of pre-schoolers can have a place in a Government supported pre-school, up from about 50% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the Government has increased the number of infant care and childcare places over the last five years, this is still woefully inadequate in towns such as Sengkang, which has the highest number of young children across Singapore by planning area with 17,000 0 to four-year-olds and about 17,000 five to nine-year-olds as of June 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What is the target total number of centres and places that will be offering infant care services and childcare services in 2025 and where will these be located?

sections.label: Evening and overnight childcare services
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will consider an islandwide network of evening and overnight childcare services for shift workers' children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider setting up an islandwide network of evening and overnight childcare services for shift workers to ensure the safety and well-being of their vulnerable children?

sections.label: MSF programme progress and expansion
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MSF can share the progress of this programme and its expansion plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: Can MSF share the progress of this programme and its expansion plans?

sections.label: Government early childhood spending
sections.summary: Government spending on early childhood care and education exceeds $1 billion annually and is growing, described as an investment in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the increasing Government spending on early childhood care and education of more than $1 billion annually and growing, it is an investment in the right direction.

sections.label: Pre-school plans and SPARK certification
sections.summary: Plans include raising Government-supported pre-schools from about 50% to 80% and enhancing subsidies, while only about 50% of pre-schools are SPARK-certified.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Plans announced so far, including increasing the number of Government-supported pre-schools from about 50% to 80% and enhancing pre-school subsidies for more families to be eligible, are all welcomed but may not be sufficient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While the Singapore Pre-school Accreditation Framework, or SPARK, is also a good tool to continually enhance and assure quality education in pre-schools, only about 50% of pre-schools are SPARK-certified so far.

sections.label: ECDA oversight and inclusive pre-schools
sections.summary: ECDA under MSF will oversee early intervention and pre-school services from end-2020, and MSF launched an inclusive pre-school workgroup.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The move for Early Childhood Development Agency, or ECDA, under MSF to oversee early intervention services and pre-school services from the end of 2020, with the transfer of early intervention functions from the Disability Office in MSF to ECDA is an encouraging move towards inclusive pre-schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MSF has also launched an inclusive pre-school workgroup to strengthen the support for children with developmental needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I will like to ask for an update on the plans and implementation for having more inclusive pre-schools in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As the third Enabling Masterplan 2017-2021 will come to an end this year, I would also like to ask MSF how it will engender more creative and impactful ways of nurturing children with disabilities from their early childhood period to better achieve their fullest potential as integral and contributing members of our society.

sections.label: Special Student Care Centres and subsidies
sections.summary: Questions are asked on SSCC enrolment, vacancy shortages, and the impact of increased subsidies and broadened income criteria under SCFA since July last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: In addition, I would like to ask if all applicants for Special Student Care Centres (SSCCs) are able to enroll?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: Is there any shortage of vacancies and, if so, how many more places will be made available in the upcoming years?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: Since July last year, MSF had increased the subsidies and broadened the income criteria so that more families qualify for the Student Care Fee Assistance (SCFA) scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee
sentences.text: Would the Ministry share an update on the impact of these changes and a summary of the profiles of the families and the children it has helped?

sections.label: Expiring plan and new plan
sections.summary: The current plan will be expiring this year and a new one is expected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The current plan will be expiring this year and a new one is expected.

sections.label: Ayden's Down Syndrome and autism
sections.summary: Ayden has Down Syndrome and was recently clinically diagnosed as being on the autism spectrum.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Ayden has Down Syndrome and was also recently clinically diagnosed as being on the autism spectrum.

sections.label: Enabling Masterplans for PWDs
sections.summary: The Enabling Masterplans and their evolution reflect Government efforts to create an inclusive environment for persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Enabling Masterplans and their evolution over the years reflect the efforts of the Government in creating an inclusive environment for persons with disabilities (PWDs).

sections.label: Challenges and bullying of PWDs
sections.summary: Some parents shared challenges finding suitable child care or pre-school nearby, and PWDs, especially those with intellectual disability, are bullied or taken advantage of.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Some parents have shared about challenges they had in finding a suitable child care or pre-school in the vicinity of their neighbourhood.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I have heard many instances of PWDs, especially those with intellectual disability, being bullied or taken advantage of in school or at work.

sections.label: Success of inclusiveness campaigns
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the different campaigns and efforts to encourage inclusiveness in the community have been successful.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Have the different campaigns and efforts to encourage inclusiveness in the community been successful?

sections.label: Typecasting PWDs into menial tasks
sections.summary: Otherwise PWDs, especially those with intellectual disabilities, will continue to be typecast into menial tasks and their full potential not tapped.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Otherwise, we will continue to typecast PWDs, especially those with intellectual disabilities to just do menial tasks and we do not get to tap on their full potential.

sections.label: Educating, integrating and embracing PWDs
sections.summary: The speaker says people behave as they do from ignorance, and calls for Government education, families of PWDs being open, and integration at policy, organisation and individual level.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I think often people behave the way they do because of ignorance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I believe the Government can play a role in educating and creating understanding, but families of PWDs also need to be open and willing to embrace people who lack understanding, not shun or criticise them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Teach them, tell them kindly about the appropriate vocabulary, the appropriate approach, the appropriate way to interact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I believe that a conscious approach of integration and inclusiveness is necessary at the policy, organisation and individual level.

sections.label: Women in leadership positions
sections.summary: DBS Bank has led with women in leadership, but gender equality in schools has not translated to leadership levels, and the passage asks what ideas emerged from the Conversations on Women's development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the private sector, organisations like DBS Bank, have led the way with several women in leadership positions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But we are still far away from translating gender equality in our schools to gender equality at the leadership levels, both senior management and Board.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Around the world, this gap has persisted for a long time, long after we have achieved gender equality in schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, it is proven that gender diversity drives performance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our companies will do better with more women in leadership positions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In addition, women leaders are important because they are role models who inspire the future generation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, out of the Conversations on Women's development, what are the emerging ideas for what more can be done to really move the needle on getting more women in leadership positions?

sections.label: Effort against traditional inequalities
sections.summary: The speaker says the effort has merit because many traditional inequalities still exist despite 50 years of progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: All these could be true, but I feel the effort itself has merit simply because despite all the progress we have made in the last 50 years, many of the traditional inequalities still exist.

sections.label: Apologies and lack of intent
sections.summary: The passage states that when apologising, one should not hide behind misunderstood intentions or ask the offended to be forgiving, as lack of malicious intent is no defence against harm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: It is important to note that when one apologises for a misstep, not just in relation on such gender biases, but in general, we should not hide behind "misunderstood" intentions, neither should we call on the person whom we offended to be gracious and "forgiving" about the matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: It is time we recognise that the lack of malicious intent offers no shield, no defence against the harm that is done.

sections.label: Women on social enterprise boards
sections.summary: The passage states 36% of board members across eight social enterprises are women, above the SID 30% target, and 50% of the NTUC group leadership team are women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The hon Member, Ms Mariam Jaafar, you will be pleased to note that across the boards of eight of our social enterprises, 36% are women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This compares favourably with Singapore Institute of Directors's (SID) target of 30% for Public Listed companies by 2030; we are already 36%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: But these numbers show that we have made progress but still have some way to go.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And again, amongst the leadership team at the NTUC group of Enterprises, 50% are women.

sections.label: Divorce effects and MSF help
sections.summary: The passage cites an MSF study on divorce effects on children, 2019 statistics of about three divorces per 10 marriages, and asks MSF for 2020 figures and earlier help for marital distress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to the MSF Study on the Inter-generational Effects of Divorce on Children in Singapore, children generally tend to suffer divorce penalties in terms of their income and academic qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to the latest divorce statistics released in 2019, there were about three divorces in every 10 marriages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Can MSF provide an update on the number of divorce cases in 2020?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Can MSF examine ways to help couples identify early signs of marriage distress, especially for the most cited reason of "unreasonable behaviour" and help resolve such marital issues earlier, rather than waiting till pre-divorce proceedings have been initiated?

sections.label: Family violence taskforce engagement plans
sections.summary: The passage asks what the plans and recommendations are for engaging stakeholders after the family violence taskforce was formed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What are the plans and recommendations for engagements with stakeholders following the formation of the taskforce to tackle family violence?

sections.label: Singapore's 1965 reserves and GDP
sections.summary: The passage states that at independence in 1965 Singapore had barely $1 billion in reserves and a GDP of about $3 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: When we became independent in 1965, we had barely $1 billion in reserves and were still negotiating for it to be in our control.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Our GDP was about $3 billion, a small fraction of what it is today.

sections.label: Preschool, post-secondary and home ownership
sections.summary: About nine in 10 Singaporean children entered Primary 1 with at least three years of preschool, 97% of resident children went on to post-Secondary education, and around 90% of resident households own their homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: About nine in 10 Singaporean children would have entered Primary 1 with at least three years in preschool, and 97% of Singaporeans and Permanent Residents' children would go on to post-Secondary education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Around 90% of Singapore resident household own their homes, with the bottom decile at close to 85%.

sections.label: Social spending doubled
sections.summary: Even before COVID-19, social spending was more than doubled in the past 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Even before COVID-19, we have more than doubled our social spending in the past 10 years.

sections.label: Care for the permanently unable
sections.summary: For those permanently unable to care for themselves and without other forms of support, the government will help care for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For those permanently unable to care for themselves and without other forms of support, we will help care for them.

sections.label: Good start for every child
sections.summary: The government will strive to give every child a good start in life, regardless of family background.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: While we have done well in some regards, we must continue to press on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We will strive to give every child a good start in life, regardless of family background.

sections.label: Scaling up KidSTART support
sections.summary: As preschool affordability, accessibility and quality are enhanced, KidSTART is being scaled up to provide additional upstream support for children from lower income families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: As we enhance the affordability, accessibility and quality of preschools for all families, we recognise that children from lower income families may require more targeted assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Hence, we are scaling up KidSTART to provide this additional upstream support.

sections.label: Third Enabling Masterplan workgroups
sections.summary: Three workgroups under the Third Enabling Masterplan look into employment, independent living and more inclusive pre-schools, with recommendations to be shared in April.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: At the national level, we have three workgroups looking into key aspects of our journey to foster stronger inclusivity in our society under our Third Enabling Masterplan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: They look into areas like employment, independent living and making our pre-schools more inclusive, and we will share their recommendations in April.

sections.label: Temporary Relief Fund disbursements
sections.summary: More than $440 million was disbursed under the Temporary Relief Fund and COVID-19 Support Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Together, more than $440 million were disbursed under the Temporary Relief Fund and COVID-19 Support Grant which provided a much-needed lifeline to many families.

sections.label: CRG and MSF job creation
sections.summary: Over 7,500 Singaporeans benefited from CRG, and MSF worked towards around 4,500 jobs and skills opportunities this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Over 7,500 Singaporeans have benefited from CRG to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: MSF, too, has supported this job creation initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We have worked towards creating around 4,500 jobs and skills opportunities by this year.

sections.label: Community Capability Trust fund
sections.summary: A new fund of up to $480 million, comprising Government funds and community donations, is being set up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We are setting up the Community Capability Trust (CCT).

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: It is a new fund of up to $480 million, comprising Government funds and community donations.

sections.label: SHARE As One extension
sections.summary: The SHARE As One programme will be extended to provide dollar-for-dollar matching for another two years till FY2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: To encourage greater giving, we will be extending the SHARE As One programme to provide dollar-for-dollar matching for another two years till FY2023.

sections.label: Government matching donations
sections.summary: The Government will match 50 cents to every dollar donated through these platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The Government will match 50 cents to every dollar donated through these platforms.

sections.label: MSF autism recommendations review
sections.summary: MSF will review the recommendations and work with friends from the autism community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: MSF will review the recommendations and is committed to working with friends from the autism community on this.

sections.label: Women's seats in Parliament
sections.summary: Women hold close to 30% of seats in this House, above the Inter-Parliamentary Union's global average of 25.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Even among this House, women occupy close to 30% of the seats, which is higher than the Inter-Parliamentary Union’s global average of 25.5%.

sections.label: Protecting women, sentencing framework
sections.summary: Misplaced attitudes must not fester, and the sentencing framework for hurt and sexual offences can be reviewed to protect women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We must not allow such misplaced attitudes to fester because they have no part in our society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: And we can do more to protect our women by reviewing the sentencing framework for hurt and sexual offences.

sections.label: Enabling women's careers, board diversity
sections.summary: Women's career development is supported while they build families, and board representation is increased through the Council for Board Diversity without perceived tokenism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: An example is that of enabling the careers of our women – supporting their career development, even while they build their families and increasing the representation of women on Boards through our Council for Board Diversity, in a manner that is not perceived as tokenism.

sections.label: Social spending before COVID-19
sections.summary: Before COVID-19, social spending had more than doubled in the past 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Previously, before COVID-19, we have more than doubled our social spending in the past 10 years.

sections.label: MSF social safety nets, 3C principles
sections.summary: MSF's transformation of social safety nets is guided by 3C principles, with the PEERS Network for rough sleepers formed in July 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: At MSF, my colleagues have been working hard to strengthen and transform our social safety nets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This transformation is guided by our 3C principles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: First, providing comprehensive support, not only downstream when issues occur, but also going upstream to identify and tackle root issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Second, ensuring that help is convenient, by putting individuals and families that we serve at the centre and organising support around their needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Third, coordinating ourselves by building strong partnerships and networks, anchored in local communities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Social Services Integration (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: One example was the PEERS Network, which stands for “Partners Engaging and Empowering Rough Sleepers”.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The PEERS Network was officially formed in July 2019, and includes Social Service Agencies (SSAs), community groups and Government agencies.

sections.label: Rough sleepers sheltered, transitional shelters
sections.summary: The Network has sheltered about 900 rough sleepers since April 2020, and two new Transitional Shelters took in about 250 residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Network has sheltered about 900 rough sleepers since April 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: MSF also set up two new Transitional Shelters in January this year, and about 250 residents from Safe Sound Sleeping Places have moved into new Transitional Shelters.

sections.label: Reaching 50,000 rental households
sections.summary: MSF, PA and MCCY rallied partners and 900 volunteers to reach 50,000 rental households, referring 5,000 to agencies for further support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: MSF, PA and MCCY rallied community partners, social service agencies, corporates and some 900 volunteers to reach out to 50,000 rental households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We managed to offer timely support, especially to households who were suffering but had not yet reached out to seek help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We referred 5,000 households in rental flats to various agencies for further healthcare support, counselling, employment and financial assistance and so on.

sections.label: Case Connect referral platform
sections.summary: Case Connect lets frontline officers and case workers make referrals, share assessments and updates, and coordinate with partners on one platform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Case Connect will allow frontline officers and case workers to make referrals, share assessments and updates, and coordinate with other partners on a single platform.

sections.label: ComLink pilot launch and families
sections.summary: In 2019 MSF launched ComLink at four pilot locations and has since supported 1,000 families with children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In 2019, MSF launched ComLink at four pilot locations: Boon Lay, Jalan Kukoh, Kembangan-Chai Chee and Marsiling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Since its launch, we have supported 1,000 families with children.

sections.label: ComLink programmes with partners
sections.summary: About 30 corporates, donors and social service agencies and 240 volunteers mounted some 60 ComLink programmes tailored to families' and community needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It might take months, it might take years, it might take even a generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We also partnered about 30 corporates, donors and social service agencies, and 240 volunteers to mount some 60 ComLink programmes specifically tailored to meet the families' and the community's needs.

sections.label: Scaling ComLink across Singapore
sections.summary: ComLink will scale over two years from four sites to 21 towns, covering 14,000 rental housing families with children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We want to empower more families like Theresa's.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will therefore scale ComLink across Singapore over the next two years to cover all families with children living in rental housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will do so by expanding from the existing four sites to 21 towns in the next two years to cover 14,000 rental housing families with children across the island.

sections.label: Four ComLink coordination approaches
sections.summary: The passage lists four approaches: streamline outreach, align agencies to common outcomes, empower lead agencies, and better signpost ground needs to donors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: First, streamline outreach efforts so that families are not overtaxed by various agencies and interventions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Second, align agencies to a common set of outcomes centred on the families so that families are not pulled in different directions by different agencies and charities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Third, empower lead agencies such as our SSOs and Family Service Centres (FSCs) to exercise more leadership to stitch together interventions while other agencies support as part of one team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Fourth, provide better signposting of ground needs to donors, to volunteers, to philanthropists and corporate social responsibility (CSR), so that their giving is not just meaningful but impactful, targeted and productive.

sections.label: Child Development Account co-matching cap
sections.summary: Minister Indranee announced an increase in the co-matching cap in the Child Development Account for the second child, and later Government-Paid Paternity and Adoption Benefit Schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Minister Indranee announced the increase in the co-matching cap in the Child Development Account for the second child.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will also introduce Government-Paid Paternity Benefit and Adoption Benefit Schemes later this year.

sections.label: Strengthening Families Programme pilot
sections.summary: In 2019, MSF piloted two Strengthening Families Programme @ Family Service Centres with Care Corner Singapore and Fei Yue Community Services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In 2019, MSF piloted two Strengthening Families Programme @ Family Service Centres, otherwise known as SFP@FSC, with Care Corner Singapore and Fei Yue Community Services.

sections.label: Divorce Support Specialist Agencies folded
sections.summary: Four existing Divorce Support Specialist Agencies will be folded into the SFP@FSC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Four existing Divorce Support Specialist Agencies, or DSSAs, will be folded into the SFP@FSC.

sections.label: Council for Board Diversity White Paper
sections.summary: The Council for Board Diversity encourages diversity and grooms board-ready women, and a White Paper will be submitted to Parliament in the second half of 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Council for Board Diversity encourages diversity in organisations and identifies and grooms potential board-ready women.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will continue to gather and study the feedback provided and submit a White Paper to the Parliament in the second half of 2021.

sections.label: Pre-school subsidy income ceiling increase
sections.summary: Since January 2020, the household income ceiling for means-tested pre-school subsidies rose to $12,000 a month, and around 78,000 children now benefit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Since January 2020, the household income ceiling for means-tested pre-school subsidies has increased to $12,000 a month, from $7,500 for childcare and infant care, and $6,000 for KiFAS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Around 78,000 children now benefit from means-tested subsidies, up from around 48,000 in 2019.

sections.label: Government funding for childcare
sections.summary: With latest subsidies and fee caps, a Singaporean child in full-day childcare for five years with an Anchor Operator benefits from about $50,000 in Government funding.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: With the latest subsidies and fee caps, a Singaporean child enrolled in full-day childcare for five years with an Anchor Operator would benefit from about $50,000 in Government funding.

sections.label: Pre-school Inclusion Coordinator appointment
sections.summary: From the second half of 2023, every pre-school will work towards appointing an Inclusion Coordinator from existing staff.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In Tier 1, we will work towards every pre-school appointing an "Inclusion Coordinator", or ICO, among existing staff, beginning in the second half of 2023.

sections.label: DS-LS expansion and I-n-S-P pilot
sections.summary: DS-LS covered about 600 pre-schools in 2020, with plans to reach 60% of pre-schoolers by 2025 and 80% at steady-state, plus a Tier 3 pilot.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In 2020, the DS-LS programme covered about 600 pre-schools which enrol over 40% of resident pre-schoolers aged five to six.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We plan to expand outreach of the DS-LS programme to more pre-schools covering 60% of pre-schoolers by 2025, and covering 80% at steady-state.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In Tier 3, we will pilot a new Inclusive Support Programme, or I-n-S-P, at a few sites with selected providers to integrate planning and provision of both early childhood and early intervention services at pre-schools for children aged three to six, who require medium levels of early intervention support.

sections.label: Expanding pilot to more regions
sections.summary: Based on good feedback, the pilot will expand to three more regions by end of this year, with the remaining five within two years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Based on good feedback from this pilot, we will expand to three more regions by the end of this year, and the remaining five will be rolled out within the next two years.

sections.label: National Committee on Prevention, Rehabilitation and Recidivism
sections.summary: The NCPR, co-chaired with Minister of State Faishal of MHA, oversees national efforts on offending, re-offending and offender rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The National Committee on Prevention, Rehabilitation and Recidivism (NCPR), which I co-chair with Minister of State Faishal of MHA, oversees national efforts to prevent offending, re-offending and to enhance rehabilitation of offenders.

sections.label: Fall in youth arrests
sections.summary: The number of youths arrested has fallen by about 40% over the last decade.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The number of youths arrested has fallen by about 40% over the last decade.

sections.label: Mentors and post-care support extension
sections.summary: Mentors will where possible pave the way for internships, apprenticeships or job placements, and post-care support for youths discharged from MSF Youth Homes was extended from two months to one year.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Where possible, mentors will pave the way for internships, apprenticeships, or job placements for these mentees.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: I am also pleased to update that from February 2021, that is last month, post-care support for our youths discharged from MSF Youth Homes has been extended from two months to one year for all youths discharged from the Homes.

sections.label: MSF investigated older children cases
sections.summary: From July to December 2020, MSF investigated 25 cases involving older children.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: From July to December 2020, MSF investigated 25 such cases involving older children.

sections.label: PEERS Network partners and volunteers
sections.summary: The PEERS Network has 35 partners running Safe Sound Sleeping Places and mobilising volunteers to reach rough sleepers.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The PEERS Network, for instance, has 35 partners who run Safe Sound Sleeping Places (S3Ps) and mobilise volunteers to reach out to rough sleepers.

sections.label: Volunteer networks public can join
sections.summary: Volunteer networks the public can join include the VIC Network, the Charity Food Workgroup and ComLink.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Other volunteer networks which the public can join include the Vulnerable-in-Community (VIC) Network, which befriends and supports vulnerable individuals, including tissue paper sellers and cardboard collectors; the Charity Food Workgroup for instance, which coordinates charity food support to beneficiaries; and the earlier-mentioned ComLink, which supports families in rental flats.

sections.label: Support system for vulnerable youth
sections.summary: The Government will work with community partners on a preventive support system for vulnerable youth and pilot a mentoring programme for students leaving ITE prematurely.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In order to bring out the best in our youth, the Government will continue to work closely with our community partners to build a preventive support system for our vulnerable youth.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We will also pilot a mentoring programme targeted at students who leave ITE prematurely.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We hope to guide them to build a network of positive relationships and also help them to find internships or job placements in the areas where they are interested in.

sections.label: Pre-school within walking distance
sections.summary: A Member asks whether the Ministry will consider a plan for every household to be within walking distance of a pre-school.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: We have some time for clarifications, if any.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: I think we have the plans to have every household be within 10 minutes walking distance of a park by 2030, so similarly, one of the common feedback that my residents have shared in terms of pre-school is that they are facing difficulties having a pre-school near their place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: So, I was just wondering if the Ministry will consider having such a plan whereby every household would be within walking distance of an available pre-school.

sections.label: Childcare capacity in Sengkang and Punggol
sections.summary: Childcare capacity in Sengkang and Punggol more than doubled in five years, and the Government will place childcare in accessible locations where possible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For new estates, like Sengkang, like Punggol, if you look at childcare's capacity, it has more than doubled in Sengkang and Punggol in the past five years from about 11,000 in 2015 to over 23,000 places today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: But I take the point that many young families would like to have a childcare as close as possible where it is logically and logistically possible because we also have to look at void deck space and the facilities that are available.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: But as a matter of principle, the Government knows the needs of young families and where it is possible, as we ramp up the total number of childcare places, we will have them in accessible locations for young families.
